reasoning_traces.think:
The Defensive Motor Index (DMI) is constructed as a composite metric to capture non-traditional defensive contributions that are otherwise invisible in standard box scores. It aggregates four key hustle-based statistics: deflections, loose ball recoveries, contested shots, and transition defensive effectiveness. Each component is assigned a weight based on empirical relevance derived from player tracking and play-by-play data. The index is formulated as a linear combination to maintain interpretability while enabling aggregation across diverse defensive actions. Its dual nature lies in its ability to both quantify individual defensive effort and serve as a predictive variable for team defensive outcomes. Failure modes include over-reliance on sparse data, misalignment of weights with actual game impact, and exclusion of positional nuances. The index must be normalized or scaled to ensure comparability across different playing styles and roles.
